About the viewer

This tool displays sea-level-rise-driven flooding in coastal Naples, Florida. It uses a simple bathtub inundation approach with a coastal-connectivity constraint to provide a first-order screening of areas that may be vulnerable to selected future water levels.

Interactive controlsUse the decade, scenario, sea-level-rise, tide, and opacity controls to compare inundation conditions.
Depth readoutHover over blue flooded cells to view water depth, DEM elevation, and selected total water level.
Satellite baselineThe inundation layer is drawn over a live satellite basemap for local context.

Method

A raster cell is first classified as potentially flooded when its ground elevation is lower than or equal to the selected water level. The presentation describes this rule as DEM ≤ SLR. In this viewer, the selected water level is the sum of sea-level rise and tide.

Total water levelSLR meters + tide meters. Tide values entered in feet are converted to meters before being added.
Potential floodingCells with DEM elevation less than or equal to the selected total water level are marked as potentially flooded.
Flood depthDepth is calculated as selected total water level minus DEM elevation.
Coastal connectivityDepth values are retained only where a cell is continuously connected to the coast/tidal water source. This removes isolated inland depressions that are low but not hydraulically connected to the Gulf.

Scenarios

The scenario controls use two IPCC CMIP6 emissions pathways and two projection decades. Selecting a decade and pathway updates the sea-level-rise value automatically. The tide slider remains editable so high-tide or other tide assumptions can be tested.

SSP2-4.5Medium-emission scenario used for the 2050 and 2100 comparison.
SSP5-8.5High-emission scenario used for the 2050 and 2100 comparison.
2050 and 2100Projection decades used to compare moderate and high future sea-level-rise conditions.

Limitations

This viewer is not a fully dynamic hydraulic model. It is a screening-level visualization of possible inundation patterns.

Uniform water levelIt does not simulate time-series tides, storm surge timing, wind setup, waves, or dynamic hydraulics.
No routing or infrastructureIt does not represent culverts, stormwater systems, channels, levees, flow resistance, or groundwater effects.
Simplified connectivityRaster neighborhood connectivity approximates pathways and may not fully capture small barriers or conveyance features.
Datum and DEM sensitivityResults depend on DEM quality, spatial resolution, vertical datum consistency, and the assumed SLR/tide datum.

About this Naples flooding tool

This simple tool displays sea-level-rise-driven flooding in coastal Naples, Florida, using a bathtub inundation approach with a coastal-connectivity constraint. It is intended as a first-order screening tool to compare possible inundation under different sea-level rise and tide combinations.

Flood ruleA raster cell is first classified as potentially flooded when its ground elevation is lower than or equal to the selected water level. In the presentation, this is expressed as DEM ≤ SLR.
Flood depthFlood depth is calculated as the selected total water level minus the DEM elevation. Depth values are shown only where the cell is part of a flooded area that remains connected to the coast.
Connectivity constraintOnly cells that are continuously connected to the Gulf/coastal water source are retained. This helps remove isolated inland depressions that are below the water level but are not hydraulically connected to the coast.
Scenarios usedThe tool uses two IPCC CMIP6 scenarios: SSP2-4.5 (medium emissions) and SSP5-8.5 (high emissions).
Decades shownScenario presets are available for 2050 and 2100. Selecting a decade and scenario automatically fills the corresponding sea-level rise value.
Tide handlingThe Tide slider remains interactive so you can explore how added tide changes the projected total water level and inundation footprint.
InterpretationThis is not a fully dynamic hydraulic model. Instead, it provides a practical screening-level visualization of areas that may be vulnerable to future inundation under moderate and high sea-level-rise conditions.

How to use the viewer

  • Select a Decade and Scenario to load the preset sea-level rise value.
  • Adjust the Sea level rise and Tide sliders to test alternative combinations.
  • Move the pointer over flooded cells to see water depth, DEM elevation, and total water level.
  • Use the opacity slider to compare the inundation overlay with the satellite basemap.

Important limitations

  • Uniform water level: the tool does not simulate tides through time, storm surge timing, wind setup, waves, or dynamic hydraulics.
  • No routing or infrastructure effects: it does not explicitly represent culverts, stormwater systems, channels, levees, or groundwater effects.
  • Simplified connectivity: raster connectivity approximates pathways and may not fully capture small barriers or conveyance features.
  • Datum and DEM sensitivity: results depend on DEM quality, spatial resolution, and vertical datum consistency.
